models_evaluated: commercially available AI lung nodule detection software (unnamed)

links.outcome: Local retrospective performance against radiologist report and cancer diagnosis reference standards
links.effect: Versus radiologist reports: sensitivity 54.5%, specificity 83.2%, PPV 5.5%, NPV 99.0%. Versus cancer diagnosis: sensitivity 60.9%, PPV 5.6%. Considerable underperformance in real-world cohort.
links.quote: The software demonstrated considerable underperformance in this real-world patient cohort.

links.outcome: Generalisability of training/testing data to local population; false positive failure analysis
links.effect: Normal or variant anatomy misidentified as abnormality in 69.9% of 943 false positives; lack of generalisability in training and testing datasets suggested as factor.
links.quote: Failure analysis suggested a lack of generalisability in the training and testing datasets as a potential factor.

links.outcome: Low PPV in low-prevalence population causing false positives and over-investigation
links.effect: PPV 5.5% with 1.6% cancer prevalence; 943 false positives; low PPV risks over-investigation and limits clinical translation.
links.quote: The low PPV carries the risk of over-investigation and limits the translation of the software to clinical practice.

screen.reason: Retrospective external validation and failure analysis of a commercial chest radiograph AI tool in a real-world primary care cohort to assess real-world diagnostic performance and safety/over-investigation risks.
